In the original it gives the Windows handle behind a gadget (query 1 is the HWND, 2 the HWND of the client area, 3 the HFONT), so it can be used with the Windows API.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 32, 2
win = CreateWindow("Query", 20, 20, 240, 100, Desktop(), 3)
SetGadgetText win, "Handle " + QueryObject(win, 1)
Repeat
Until WaitEvent() = $803
```
@param object  A window, gadget or font.
@param query   1 for the window handle, 2 for the client handle, 3 for the font handle.
@gap All gadgets are drawn inside the one window of the program, so queries 1 and 2 give the handle of that window (an HWND on Windows) for every gadget. Fonts (3) have no handle of the operating system and give 0, and so does anything that is not a gadget.
@returns The handle of the system that the query asks for, or 0 if the object has none (see the difference below).
